links.reason: Verse 2 says the slips of the praiser's own speech are not slips (வாய்க்குற்ற சொல்லின் வழுவும் வழு அல்ல) because of what is praised; verse 17 says a fault in the exalted stays a fault (குற்றங் குற்றமே நல்ல வாகா). One is about faults of wording in a praise-poem, the other about faults in the persons praised, so these are different situations rather than incompatible claims about the same thing; the teaches' conclusion that the apology 'rests on devotion, not on a rule' is built on that overstated conflict.

The agreement is real: உணர்ச்சி யில்லோர் உடைமை உள்ளேம்; நல்லறிவுடையோர் நல்குரவு உள்ளுதும் ... உவந்து sets the riches of the unfeeling below the poverty of the wise, as Kural 408 sets கல்லார்கண் பட்ட திரு below நல்லார்கண் பட்ட வறுமை. But teaches claims the maxim 'was first' a bard's claim, a priority of date neither text establishes, and 197's point is what the poet esteems in a patron (பாடறிந்து ஒழுகும் பண்பு), not which state is more painful.

Both verses set தவம் against பொருளொடு போகம்: 20 bids those joined to wealth and pleasure still do அருந்தவம், 42 says one without தவம் toils for wealth and pleasure like ploughing without seed (வித்தின்றிப் பைங்கூழ் விளைக்குறல்). The pair genuinely adds up to tavam as both the duty of the prosperous and the seed of prosperity, which neither verse says alone.
links.text_issue: Both verses carry the -ளடு flag (பொருளடு for பொருளொடு); the reading as 'with' is clearly intended in both.

links.reason: The fragment's பொறைமைஇல் நோன்பும் ... இருளினுள் இட்ட இருண்மை does make forbearance a condition of the vow, a stronger claim than the Kural's ranking (உண்ணாது நோற்பார் பெரியர் ... இன்னாச்சொல் நோற்பாரின் பின்). But the epic-side gain says the Kural supplies 'the reason why bearing insult is the harder discipline', and 160 gives no reason, only a rank; and the other-side gain presents the fragment as reading the couplet, with no shared wording to show it.

The contrast is real: the fragment's சேயிலாச் செல்வம் is one item in a list of things lacking their completion, while the Kural's அறிவறிந்த மக்கட்பேறு praises children conditioned on understanding. But neither limits the other, so QUALIFIES fits loosely, and the epic-side gain (that the fragment values the child only relative to wealth) is visible from the fragment alone and overstates a simile list whose subject is wealth.

The words are close: the fragment's மாரி பெருகப் பெருகி அறவறும் and வாரி ... சுருங்கி against the quatrain's மாரி அறவே அறுமே ... வாரி அறவே அறும், the same river-and-income simile with வாரி doing double duty. The quatrain gives only the cutting-off; the fragment adds the rise (வாரி பெருகப் பெருகிய காதல்), so teaches is true and specific, and the note rightly says 'lie close' rather than 'quote'.

Lines 1-2 (மற்றும் தொடர்ப்பா(டு) எவன்கொல் பிறப்(பு)அறுக்கல் உற்றார்க்(கு) உடம்பு மிகை) are Kural 345 almost word for word, a genuine quotation. Lines 3-4 add the reason the couplet leaves unstated, that while these remain karma clings (பற்றா வினையாய்) and the soul wanders through many wombs (பலபல யோனிகள்), so the development and both gains hold.

Both start from wealth that does not stay (ஈண்டல் அரிதாய்க் கெடுதல் எளிதாகி; யார்மாட்டும் நில்லாது செல்வம் சகடக்கால் போல வரும்) and draw different conclusions: share it with many (பல்லாரோ டுண்க) against never wanting it (வேண்டாது ஒழிந்தார் விறலோ விழுமிதே). Teaches names the divergence specifically, and the fragment's renouncer's conclusion does limit the householder's.

The fragment shares the couplet's three terms, the day, life and the blade: நாளடி யிடுதல் தோன்றும் ... உயிர் பருகும் கூற்றின் வாளின் வாய் against நாளென ஒன்றுபோற் காட்டி உயிர் ஈரும் வாள். It adds the condemned man's walk to the killing ground with no return (மீட்சியொன்றானும் இல்லா), which is a real extension of the couplet's still image.
links.text_issue: Stanza rejoined from 8 half-lines; the join does not affect the link.

links.reason: The shared claim, that the poor man's learning or words fail (புல்லென்று போதல்; சொற்பொருள் சோர்வு படும்), is real. But teaches and the other-side gain rest on reading நல்லவை in line 2 as 'the assembly of the good'; on the plain division the line says no one esteems the good things (நல்லவை) the poor have understood, and the named hearers disappear. A link needing that generous reading is weak.

Verse 18's maxim (அழுங்கார் உவவார் உறுவது உறும்) is tested in 19 by a man who neither swells nor wilts (பூரித்தல் வாடுதல் ... பொலிவின்றி நின்றான்) through a release and a death plot. 19 names the cause 18 leaves unnamed: பாரித்ததெல்லாம் வினையின் பயன். That is fulfilment, not story order, and the link does not need the lost plot.
links.text_issue: Verse 19's sense is flagged uncertain; who plots the killing is not stated, but the link does not depend on it.

links.reason: The note is accurate: the Kural's tongue is speech (சொல்லிழுக்கு), while the fragment's is one of the இந்திரியம் ஐந்து, so it covers taste. But the other-side gain says the couplet is 'shown being reread', and nothing in the fragment's words (காக்கப் படுவன ... நாக்கு அல்லது இல்லை) shows it reading Kural 127; teaches' last clause also leans on the editor's grouping with the flesh verses.

அருள்இல் அறன் as darkness and அருளாதான் செய்யும் அறம் as a muddled man seeing truth make the same claim, so this is agreement more than development. The epic-side gain says the fragment gains 'the Kural's fuller case for grace as the root of virtue', but 249 makes no such case; that is a commentator's conclusion, as the marker's own nuance admits.

The fragment grants the courtesan the outward form of the wife's service (எத்திறத் தானும் வழிபட்டு ஒழுகலின் ... பத்தினிப் பெண்டிர் படியும் புரைப) on the condition of wealth (ஒத்த பொருளான்). The quatrain's wife places the difference in a shyness that is renewed every time (அஞ்ஞான்று கண்டேம்போல் நாணுதும்) against those who embrace many for gain (பொருள்நசையால் பன்மார்பு). So the pairing locates the difference where neither text alone does.

The quatrain's last line, செத்தாரைச் சாவார் சுமந்து, makes the mourners the dying. The fragment carries that inward: பாளை, பாலன், காளை and youth have each died (செத்தும்), so we die daily (நாளுநாட் சாகின்றாம்). The added measure, a death at every stage of growth, is specific and true of the words.

The venba's கண்ணீர் is only one of four things the king sees (பொடி, கருங்குழல், தனிச்சிலம்பு, கண்ணீர்), and it is her words entering his ear (சொற்செவியில் உண்டளவே) that take his life. So 'tears ... take the king's life' overstates, and the Kural's tears are those of the afflicted under a harsh rule (அல்லற்பட்டு ஆற்றாது அழுத), not a wronged suitor's. The episode mostly illustrates the couplet; teaches names a difference (slow wearing against instant death), but the link is a bridge with no gains given.
links.text_issue: Bridge to the Kural printed with no gains clause.

links.reason: Verse 3 credits the பத்தினி with public praise and rain at her word (பெய்கெனப் பெய்தலும்); verse 4 says garlanded women's hearts melt for another even with Kaman (காமனொடு ஆயினும் உள்ளம் பிறிதாய் உருகலும்). Read as about women generally (கோதையர்), 4 is incompatible with 3's chaste wife, and the note and teaches state that this reading is what the conflict depends on and that the two may be in different mouths.

Verse 49 lists பத்தினி among the old courtesan's models and says these are best opened out elsewhere (வேறோர் இடத்து வெளிப்பட நன்றாம்); 57 is that opening out: பத்தினிப் பெண்டிர் படியும் புரைப, serving in every way those who give matching wealth (ஒத்த பொருளான்). The later verse fulfils a promise the earlier one makes, and the teaches' explanation of the satire is true of 57's words.

The opposition is partly real: Kundalakesi 4 puts பொடித்துகள் மெய்பூசல் among the practices it calls words (வார்த்தை இவை), while Tirumanthiram 1662 makes பூதி அணிவது the first emblem. But 1662's சாதனம் is an emblem of the yogi, not a claim that the mark is the tapas, so the 'disagreement on whether an outward mark can belong to tapas' is sharper than either text. The other-side gain invents a cause (Tirumular defending the emblem against attacks from outside) that neither verse states.
links.text_issue: Verse 4's sense is flagged uncertain, and பொடி may be dust rather than sacred ash.

links.reason: The shared demand-and-price argument is real (அவாவிலையின் உண்பான் against விலைப்பொருட்டால் ஊன்றருவார்). But the teaches' added point, the trapper's own interest in more deaths so that guilt runs both ways, rests wholly on line 4's மாண்டருகல் வேண்டும், which more naturally says the seller too must perish or dwindle than that he wants more creatures dead. A link built on a loose reading of an obscure line is weak.
links.text_issue: Line 4 (விற்பானு மாண்டருகல் வேண்டும்) is obscure and possibly corrupt.

links.reason: Neelakesi 9 only names ஊன்கொண்ட காட்சி as the first of the views the heroine broke; it states no argument about flesh for the fragment to develop or be developed by. What joins the two is the shared topic of flesh-eating, and teaches ('a dividing line between schools') is only that theme stated generally.

The link rests only on the number three: குற்றம் மூன்றும் அறுத்தான் names no faults, and nothing in the verse ties them to the Kural's காமம் வெகுளி மயக்கம் rather than to any other triad. The clauses are true as possibilities, but supplying the naming from outside makes this a thin connection.
links.text_issue: Kural 360 is printed with a corruption: இநவ்முன்றன் for இவ்மூன்றன்.

links.reason: The shared signs are real: நரை as messenger and the staff (கோற்கண் நெறிகாட்ட; கோல்ஊன்றி), with renunciation dated by age in one and by foresight in childhood (குழவி யிடத்தே) in the other. But teaches says the man turns 'when desire has already left him', while the line says women's desire for him has gone as he still desires (மடவார் விழைவு ஒழிய யாம் விழைய); his own desire has not left.

Both are the poet's apology to the assembly: the Kundalakesi poet says his slips are not slips (வழுவும் வழு அல்ல), the Neelakesi poet, citing the moon's spot, says he will own a fault (குற்றம் எனில் யானும் ஒட்டாமை உண்டோ). These are opposite postures in a convention, a difference of stance rather than incompatible claims, and nothing in Neelakesi 6 answers the Kundalakesi, so teaches' 'the debate between the books begins' here is overstated.

The fragment says the learned found there is no guarding women (பெண்டிரைக் காப்பது இலம்), while the Kural says the guard that keeps their own steadiness is best (நிறைகாக்கும் காப்பே தலை). As the teaches itself says, the fragment refuses the Kural's answer rather than limiting it, so the pair is a tension on a defensible reading; under QUALIFIES it is weak.

Kural 144 does not mention Indra; the shared figure exists only in Parimelazhagar's illustration of both verses, which the brief does not admit as a source. The link joins two couplets by a commentator's story, and teaches ('neither verse tells it') is false for 25, which names இந்திரன்.

The shared contemplation is real: vultures and dogs tearing the praised body (பாறொடு நாய்கள் அசிப்ப) against vultures pecking the stinking cart (வன்கழுகு ... குத்தும் முடைச்சாகாடு). But the contrast teaches and gains draw depends on the quatrain's body being a woman's, and the quatrain says only those who praise sandal paste and garlands (படுசாந்தும் கோதையும்), with no sex named. The fragment's male shoulders (மந்தரம், எழு) are real, but the quatrain did not depend on a woman's body to begin with.

Kapilar's நள்ளி நளிமுகை உடைந்த நறுங்கார் அடுக்கத்து ... காந்தள் ... புதுமலர் நாறும் நறுநுதல் and Paranar's நள்ளி சோலை அடுக்கத்து ... கடவுட் காந்தள் ... ஆய்மலர் நாறி both make the kaanthal of Nalli's slopes the measure of the woman's fragrance. Two poets using the patron's hill and flower gives a meaningful shared image, and teaches says so specifically.

Verses 4 and 46 share a view of women's minds: they turn to the new (வெள்ளம் புதியது காணின்), and once divided they cannot be gathered back (எண்ணெய் ... ஈட்டற்கு இவறுதல்). But 46 neither answers nor fulfils 4. Teaches' 'completes its case for giving them up' assumes an argument sequence the fragments do not state, so the link is a shared theme.

Verse 19 forbids eating flesh from craving (ஊன்விழைந்து உண்ணன்மின்) and promises good births, but verse 9 says nothing of flesh. Its tongue sends one to புலைநகரம் for unspecified faults, so 'the craving tongue is the flesh-eating one' is the link's own construction, built on the editor's order and a hint in புலை.

The akam heroine quotes the man's reason (தம்நயந்து உறைவோர்த் தாங்கி ... நகுதல் ஆற்றார் நல்கூர்ந்தோர்) and judges his heart as setting grace aside (அருள்பிறிது). Verse 44 states the same case directly: kin's wasting hunger relieved (அலந்த கிளைகள் அழிபசி தீர்க்கும்) and the hard wasteland crossed, asking 'is there any shame?' (புன்கண்மை உண்டோ). Each supplies the other's missing side, so teaches and both gains hold.
links.text_issue: Verse 44's sense is flagged uncertain (line 1's subject), but the kin-feeding reason the link uses is clear.

links.reason: Verse 37 bids one make provision for the next state like farmers who plough, sow and water (விளைநிலம் உழுவார்போல் வித்துநீர் செய்துகொண்மின்); verse 42's ploughman toils without seed (வித்தின்றிப் பைங்கூழ்) as the man without tavam. The same farming image is used both ways, and the shared point, that the seed of merit and not the labour decides, is meaningful.

இல்லெனின் வாழ்க்கையும் இல்லை grants the Kural's premise, பொருளில்லார்க்கு இவ்வுலகம் இல்லை, and then adds what the couplet leaves out: with it base men kill (கொல்வர் கயவர்), and had or lacked it shows itself paltry for this world and the next (இம்மை மறுமைக்கும் புல்லென்று காட்டும்). That is a real limit on the premise, as teaches and gains say.
links.text_issue: Line 2 (கொளப்பட்டும் வீடுவர்) is compressed and the verse's sense is flagged uncertain.

links.reason: The fragment says sin born of attachment cannot be removed while standing in attachment, like washing blood with blood (பற்றினான் ஆகிய பாவத்தை ... பற்றொடு நின்று). The Kural commands holding to the attachment of the one who has none (பற்றுக பற்றற்றான் பற்றினை). The simile is about the same substance cleansing itself, and the Kural's பற்று is to a different object, so the fragment does not plainly deny that devotion to the unattached can free one. The conflict needs a stretched reading of the fragment, not only of the Kural.

Verse 44 justifies wealth-seeking by the hunger of struggling kin (அலந்த கிளைகள் அழிபசி தீர்க்கும்); verse 45 shows the kin, once he is ruined, scorning him and standing out of reach (பெரிதிகழ்ந்து ... எட்டவந்தோர் இடத்து ஏகிநிற்ப). The later verse reverses the earlier's assumption of a bond, which is a limit and not mere adjacency.

Kural 796 grants ruin one benefit, a rod that measures kin (கிளைஞரை நீட்டி அளப்பதோர் கோல்); verse 45 gives the measuring in full, the kin who were no friends (நட்டவர் அல்லார்) speaking as they please. The fragment offers no 'உறுதி', so the pair shows the cost the couplet's consolation passes over, which is what teaches says.

Both start from crowned heads brought low and rebuke those who see it unchanged (மத்தக மாண்பழிதல் கண்டால் மயங்காதே; கண்டு பின்னும்). Pattinathar's remedy is reaching the feet of the Lord of the golden hall (பொன்னினம்பலவர் அடிசார்ந்து நாமுய்ய), while the fragment's is the heart's own effort in the highest path leading to சித்தி (நின்று ஊக்கஞ் செய்தியேல் சித்தி படர்தல்). Release by grace against release by one's own striving is the incompatible claim the brief names, on the reading the note states.

claims.gist: the wise gave up women earlier, finding no skill to manage them, though men manage kings and snakes

claims_rejected.why: snake charmers making snakes dance: part of the comparison

claims.gist: those who keep away from others' ill-gotten wealth escape great sorrow

claims_rejected.why: those who say there is a dharma apart: obscure

units.note: The verse is compressed and the claim is read tentatively.

claims.gist: courtesans' love takes the shape of whatever wealth is given, as the lute plays as the bard handles it

claims_rejected.why: the bard and his lute are the simile
a pastoral evening scene (calves, cow bells, cowherds' flutes): description, no claim

claims.gist: poverty is disgrace and possession brings fear to life
the renunciation of those who never took up wealth is excellent

claims_rejected.why: wealth gives little permanence and much delusion: part of the case for line 4
the old courtesan's instruction to behave like the monkey and the bee: an instruction by a character, glossed elsewhere, not a doctrinal claim

claims.gist: thieves, as the fruit of taking others' goods, are seized and have their hands and feet cut

claims_rejected.why: the fruit of theft is stated through the punishment, folded into line 4

claims.gist: people gather round even a slave who has food, and leave even the excellent once their wealth is gone, like birds at a fruiting and a fallen tree

claims_rejected.why: the bird simile illustrates the claim

claims.gist: one who gives up falsehood and practises dharma without doubt reaches a world free of pain

claims_rejected.why: the injunction to leave falsehood is the condition of the same claim

claims.gist: those who hold these (avoiding mockery and enmity) as great do not perish but live in heaven

claims_rejected.why: laughter is bad, sulking good: obscure items folded into the claim

claims.gist: bearing children and practising household dharma is the chief virtue, say those who know
spending one's life with deceitful courtesans brings no honour

claims_rejected.why: the courtesans' description is an epithet

claims.gist: in the sea of births none is free of the fault of harming others
those who eat flesh without regard for dharma have eaten their own kin from past births

claims_rejected.why: 'if one examines' is the frame, not a claim

claims.gist: the words of the teachers of faultless principle are not false: one who has done neither gift nor penance has no escape

claims_rejected.why: is there escape for us: a question, folded into line 4

units.note: A first-person lament; the speaker's own stance, so tagged reported.

claims.gist: excessive love brings suffering known to the whole land

claims_rejected.why: the lovesick laugh, weep and go sleepless: symptoms described, not separate claims

claims.gist: by the force of many deeds the soul takes body after body and suffers in many births
human birth is rare, and even when born, wealth to enjoy is rare too

claims_rejected.why: the rarity of wealth is the second half of the line 3 claim

claims.gist: when lust takes firm hold men ride the palmyra horse in public and act as if possessed

claims_rejected.why: the madal ride itself: description of the claim's content

claims.gist: do not steal anything
do not accept a dharma that comes with killing
do not associate with another man's wife

claims_rejected.why: do not despise anyone as poor: a further injunction of the list

units.note: Line 2's 'dharma joined with killing' may glance at sacrificial rites, but no school is named.

claims_rejected.why: the Nigantha sages who wipe away sorrow: an epithet inside a narrative action, not a stated claim

claims.gist: show grace to all living beings
rid yourselves of deceit and pride and keep these virtues as your wealth

claims_rejected.why: line 2 is unclear

claims.gist: one without true knowledge teaching the path of release to one who does not know is like the blind showing the blind the way

claims_rejected.why: the destroyer of former faults: an epithet

claims.gist: those who would escape the endless sorrow of wandering in the four states of birth must give up deceitful killing, said the knowers

claims_rejected.why: winning lasting fame: the first motive in the same claim

claims.gist: lust decides without thought, heeds no wise counsel and brings down those who desire much

claims_rejected.why: the separate traits of lust are folded into the one claim

claims.gist: when Kama's arrow strikes, men ignore blame, refuse elders' words and stain their fame

claims_rejected.why: the separate effects are folded into the one claim

claims.gist: there is one in the world with the strength to remove fearful sorrow

claims_rejected.why: do not rejoice thinking many will come: an injunction, obscure

units.note: The 'one' may be the Jina, but no school or name is given.

claims.gist: courtesans leave a spent man for one with greater wealth, like beasts moving to new pasture when the grass is gone

claims_rejected.why: the grazing beast is the simile

claims.gist: no one escapes Death, who never pities even once those who always obey him

claims_rejected.why: snakes, demons and lions do little harm if approached: the foil of the same claim
